correctness.rationale: For 12 vertices the domain is precisely all 4096 bit patterns on each of the 25 graphs; there are no hidden parameters. The source lists all 24 undirected edges and the integer majority/tie map. I rebuilt an entirely separate 4096-state map and path-to-cycle census for all 24 deletions plus the original: baseline (234 fixed,136 two-cycles,max depth7,32 maximizing,basin2906); class representatives (0,1),(0,6),(2,3),(2,6),(2,8) have (118,82,11,24,3164),(130,106,8,2,3094),(126,118,7,20,3032),(106,78,7,8,2996),(144,128,8,4,3080), respectively. All possible least periods were 1 or 2. The source separately enumerates the graph automorphism edge orbits of sizes (4,8,4,4,4), so positivity of all five basin differences proves universal all-edge claim. The finite domain is exhaustively enumerated, not sampled.

value.rationale: A famous smallest regular triangle-free four-chromatic graph is a natural finite stress test of majority dynamics; the every-edge consensus gain with an enlarged worst transient is a nontrivial exact graph-specific robustness phenomenon and the complete basin census is reusable, notwithstanding no global monotonicity theorem.

limitations: Exactly the provided 12-vertex labelled Chvatal graph and its 24 single deletions; no general graph edge-monotonicity statement.
